newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures end firm, seen range-bound.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures end firm, seen range-bound.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed firmer after lacklustre trade on Tuesday, helped by a rise in the dollar against the yen and a small increase in the metal's value on LME during Asian trading hours, traders said.

"We've seen directionless trade amid uncertainties over the foreign exchange rate," said one trader. "We also have to say the metal doesn't look good on the LME from a technical point of view. Prices are likely to stay within the recent trading range in near future."

Traders ascribed the firmness to rises in the LME prices since London's close on Friday. It stood at $1637/42 per tonne at 0650 GMT, compared with $1,633 at afternoon kerb close in London on Friday. The dollar's advance to above 116 yen also helped, traders added.
TOCOM benchmark April 1998 closed 1.7 yen higher at 195.7 yen per kg, while others were 1.1 to 2.2 yen stronger.
Estimated volume shrank further to a record low 1,671 lots.
Volume diminished partly because of an extended weekend in Britain and in the United States.
It stood at 1,975 lots on Monday.
